name: Weekly burst-firing, both temporal lobes, 30 min (Baker-Price & Persinger)
origin: Baker-Price & Persinger, Persinger/Koren lab, Laurentian University
summary: The bilateral-temporal arm of Baker-Price & Persinger's open-label studies of depression after closed head injury: 30 min of 1 uT burst-firing fields across both temporal lobes, once a week for 5 weeks (1996, 4 patients) or 6 weeks (2003, 14 patients). The authors reported lower depression scores, but there was no sham arm and the left-frontal arm improved as much.
notes: Baker-Price & Persinger 1996 gave four patients "30 min. of weak (1 microT) burst-firing magnetic fields across the temporal lobes once per week for 5 weeks" and reported less depression and fewer phobias, while physical symptoms did not change; their rationale was that the depression reflects subclinical hippocampal-amygdaloid seizure activity. In 2003, 14 patients got the fields either across the temporal lobes (this program) or over the left frontal lobe (persinger-tbi-depression-left-frontal), 30 min once a week for 6 weeks: depression fell over 5 weeks of treatment and 6 weeks of follow-up with no significant difference between the arms, and only the 7 bilateral-temporal patients reported fewer complex-partial-epileptic-like experiences and showed more 16-18 Hz power 6 weeks after the last session. Approximations: the burst-firing point values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) stands in: 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s, the best-supported of the lab's 230, 248 and 289-point lengths) once every 4 s; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009 describe the field as "once every 3 s for about 0.7 s" (set gapMs to 2310 for that variant). The papers give no coil count or sites; two coils per side at T7, TP7 and T8, TP8, all driven together, are an inference from "across the temporal lobes" (the same exposure as persinger-koren-boxes-tsang-2004). A Saroka thesis recalls 50 min per week; the published 30 min is used. Source cautions: no sham arm, 4 and 14 patients, self-rated outcomes in an open series where improvement over weeks is expected anyway, no independent replication; and rats given the same weekly field spent about half as much time in the open arms of a plus maze after two sessions, an anxious-looking effect (Fitzpatrick & Persinger 2004). These were clinical research sessions on diagnosed patients under ethics review. This program is not a treatment: depression and head injury need a clinician. A head injury raises seizure risk; not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed, in a quiet room. The studies were an outpatient clinical series with depression questionnaires before and after (and QEEG in 2003).
schedule: 30 min once a week for 5 weeks (1996) or 6 weeks (2003), followed in 2003 by 6 weeks without sessions.
